result.title: Beyond Reward Scoring: Online Multi-Agent Preference Learning for Multimodal Response Generation
result.summary: Multimodal preference alignment often follows a score-based RLHF pipeline: a reward model is first trained to learn human preferences, then used to score on-policy responses and optimize the response model's generation. This turns preference supervision into a scalar signal for generation: a model may learn to produce answers with higher preference scores, but is rarely trained explicitly to learn the reasons underlying human preferences. We therefore ask whether making preference understanding an internal capability of the response model can improve its generation. To investigate this question, we propose \textbf{PrefMind}, an online dual-agent reinforcement learning framework with two trainable agents: a response Generator and a preference Critic. Given a pair of candidate responses, the agents analyze and discuss which response better aligns with human preference. Human labels supervise their judgments and corrections. For pairs on which both the Generator and revised Critic correctly identify the human-preferred response, the Generator produces an improved answer, and the Critic compares it against the original preferred response to provide a generation reward. Both agents are jointly updated from interactions sampled with their current policies. Through this process, \textbf{PrefMind} trains the Generator to understand human preferences via explicit judgment and correction, and to translate this understanding into better responses. Experiments across three model scales show improvements in both standalone preference judgment and downstream response generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PrefMind：一个在线双智能体强化学习框架，含可训练的回复 Generator 与偏好 Critic，两者对候选回复进行讨论、判断与修正，由人工标签监督；在双方都能正确判别的样本上，Generator 生成改进答案、Critic 给出生成奖励，从而把偏好理解内化为生成器自身能力，在三个模型规模上同时提升偏好判断与回复生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 用可训练 Critic 与 Generator 的讨论-修正把外部标量奖励转为模型内部能力，可能为 LVR 中推理监督、贡献分配与「答案是否真正使用内部状态」的核查提供借鉴线索；但论文聚焦多模态偏好对齐而非视觉推理，迁移性需进一步核查。
